title: What does a dot plot show and hide?
description: The twenty four onion prices are drawn as dots on one number line. The board reads the spread and the stacks, and Keeko doubts that the plot can tell the price in a given month.
teaching_notes: One idea: a dot plot places each value as a dot by its size, so it shows spread, clusters and the smallest and largest values, but it loses the order of the months. Watch for students who try to read a month off a dot.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Wahapur's prices are more spread out; the months cannot be read from the plot
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Wahapur is more spread out.
The dot plot also shows the smallest and the largest prices at a glance.
It cannot tell us the month of any price.

marks.doubt: the bubble points at the green dot at 25 with the word January

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the dot plot shows January's price, because every price has a dot.
The dots are placed by price, from small to large.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The months fall away when we do that, so a dot cannot tell its month.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>A dot plot shows the spread, but not the order.
